LESSON: WRITING 5.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do you enjoy listening to stories?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing
2. create a narrative composition of about 60-80 words for self-expression

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 5.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 5.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a narrative composition of about 60-80 words for self-expression

What this means
In this part you learn to create a narrative composition of about 60-80 words for self-expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a narrative composition of about 60-80 words for self-expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a narrative composition of about 60-80 words for self-expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing to a partner. (skill: create a narrative composition of about 60-80 words for self-expression)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing.
3. Practise this skill: create a narrative composition of about 60-80 words for self-expression.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do you enjoy listening to stories?
2. Why is it important to plan our composition?
3. How can you write an interesting composition?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing.
5. Be able to: create a narrative composition of about 60-80 words for self-expression.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
